{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-in-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"9a5c6a5c3fe01c5a31069a5d12c4f97815eff53fff4357e7c3306fc4e02faf7e","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","source_liveness_sha256":"4d2b75b9a10fb774f53fb2d906a3a7a7f75f5e9387f8b4ddcd423e9b7828d59b"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Obtaining a new Indiana credential: credential types, Real ID, residency, learner's permits, vision and the two exams","heading":"C — Obtaining a new credential: credential types, Real ID, residency and new residents, ID cards, learner's permits, supervised practice, vision screening, the knowledge exam and the driving skills exam","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Obtaining a new credential: credential types, Real ID, residency and new residents, ID cards, learner's permits, supervised practice, vision screening, the knowledge exam and the driving skills exam
Knowledge domain: what a first-time Indiana applicant must know before and while getting a permit and license — the three credential types, Real ID, who counts as a resident, the rules for new residents, identification cards, learner's permit eligibility and supervised practice, the vision screening, when the knowledge exam is required and how the driving skills exam works.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
The Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles issues three kinds of credentials: identification cards, learner's permits and driver's licenses. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
An identification card costs nothing for a person who is already 18 or will turn 18 on or before the next General or Municipal Election. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Credentials for Indiana residents under 21 use a vertical layout and print the dates on which the holder turns 18 and 21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
A star in the upper right corner shows that a credential is Real ID-compliant and can serve as identification for federal purposes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
If the BMV finds that an applicant already holds a credential from another state, territory, DC or Puerto Rico, that card must be surrendered before the Indiana application is processed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The federal Real ID Act of 2005 set minimum standards so that compliant state credentials can be used for federal purposes such as boarding commercial flights or entering military and other secure federal sites. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Indiana has met the Real ID Act requirements since January 1, 2010. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Federal agencies such as DHS and TSA accept only Real ID-compliant licenses and ID cards for entry to federal facilities, TSA airport checkpoints included. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
A non-compliant Indiana credential can be upgraded to Real ID during a renewal, amendment or replacement, using original documents or certified copies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
For a Real ID upgrade the branch visit must include documents proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and Indiana residency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
Only legal Indiana residents can obtain an Indiana credential; residency can be shown by keeping an Indiana home address without claiming another state, by being registered to vote in Indiana, or by having a dependent enrolled in an Indiana elementary or secondary school. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
For credential purposes, college students and active-duty service members who do not claim Indiana residency, temporary employees and anyone not intending Indiana to be a permanent home are not treated as residents. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
A person who becomes an Indiana resident has 60 days to get an Indiana driver's license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Indiana residents may hold only one credential at a time, even when the other one came from another state, so any other credential is surrendered when applying. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
A new resident who has never held a valid license from another state must hold an Indiana learner's permit for 180 days before applying for a driver's license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
A new resident aged 18 or older with a valid out-of-state license brings one of three items: that license, a copy of the official driving record, or a verification letter. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
A knowledge exam is required when the out-of-state license expired less than five years ago or has been held unrevoked for less than one year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
When the out-of-state license has been expired for more than five years, the applicant must pass both a knowledge exam and a driving skills test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
A transferring applicant under 18 must be older than 16 years and 180 days and have held a valid out-of-state license for at least 180 days, and must also pass a knowledge exam and a vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
An identification card can be issued to an Indiana resident of any age who does not hold a driver's license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
An ID card holder aged at least 15 who passes an MDC knowledge exam receives an MDC endorsement on the card and may operate a motor driven cycle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
An identification card and an MDC endorsement are valid for six years, but cards for lawful temporary residents expire on the end-of-stay date. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A03
An applicant aged 16 or older gets a learner's permit by proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency with Appendix A documents and passing a vision screening and a knowledge exam. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
An applicant under 16 must be at least 15 and show a Certificate of Driver Education Enrollment from a BMV-licensed behind-the-wheel provider, dated no more than three weeks before the class starts. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
The certificate of completion from an online theoretical course is not accepted as proof of driver education enrollment. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
A learner's permit applicant younger than 18 must name an emergency contact who is at least 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A04
A permit holder under 16 who is enrolled in driver education may drive with a licensed driver training instructor or a BMV-recognized certified driver rehabilitation specialist sitting in the front passenger seat. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A04
A permit holder under 18 may practice with a relative by blood, marriage or legal status who is at least 25 and holds valid driving privileges, or with a licensed spouse who is at least 21, seated in the front passenger seat. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A04
A permit holder aged 18 or older may practice only with a validly licensed driver who is at least 25, or with a licensed spouse who is at least 21. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A04
Learner's permits are valid for two years from the issue date, except that permits for lawful temporary residents end on the end-of-stay date. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A04
Renewing a learner's permit that has been expired for more than 180 days requires retesting. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A04
Every permit or license applicant, renewals included, must pass a vision screening unless eligible to renew online, and drivers who wear glasses or contacts should say so and wear them for the screening. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A04
Failing the branch vision screening can lead to further evaluation, and Driver Ability may still require more testing even when the customer brings a doctor's letter. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A05
The knowledge exam is a multiple-choice test drawn from Indiana law, defensive driving practices and this manual, and it expects you to read and understand regulatory, warning and traffic signs and signals. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A05
The knowledge exam is required for permit applicants, new residents whose out-of-state license is expired or who hold a valid out-of-country license, new residents under 18 with an out-of-state license, and residents whose Indiana license expired more than 180 days ago. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A05
A driver renewing a license with six or more active points on the Indiana record must also take the knowledge exam. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A05
To take the computer-based knowledge exam the same day you must arrive at least 30 minutes before the branch closes, and after a failure you must wait until the next business day to retake it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A05
A permit holder can take the driving skills exam at a participating BMV-licensed driver training school after finishing a course of 30 hours of theory and six hours behind the wheel, and that result stays valid until the permit expires. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A05
The skills exam must be taken at a BMV branch instead if the student fails either part of the driver education course or the school does not take part in the skills test program. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A05
A BMV driving skills exam can be booked no more than three weeks and no less than 48 business hours in advance, the applicant supplies the vehicle, and the BMV charges nothing for it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A06
Only the BMV examiner or other authorized BMV staff may ride in the vehicle during the driving skills exam. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A06
The test vehicle must be legally equipped, insured, safe and clean, and its current registration must be shown before the exam. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A06
The examiner may reject a vehicle, for example one that is not properly registered or has unsafe tires, a missing bumper, broken glass or mirrors, or a door that does not work. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F44 | anchor: A06
The examiner does not teach during the exam but scores the drive objectively on a standardized form, after asking a few required questions. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

Misconceptions: a valid out-of-state license does not let a new resident skip Indiana entirely, because a vision screening and documents are always required and an exam may be too; a doctor's letter does not guarantee a pass after a failed vision screening; a learner's permit applicant under sixteen must show enrollment, not an online course completion certificate; the skills exam vehicle can be rejected before the drive starts.
Mnemonics: one person, one credential; a star means Real ID; under-sixteen permit equals fifteen plus enrolled; practice partner is twenty-five, or a spouse at twenty-one.
Glossary: credential means an identification card, learner's permit or driver's license; Real ID-compliant means meeting the federal standard for federal identification; MDC means motor driven cycle; Certificate of Driver Education Enrollment means the school's proof that behind-the-wheel training has been booked; Driver Ability means the BMV unit that can require further driving evaluation.
Dynamic facts: the BMV phone number, REALID.IN.gov, the list of driver training schools and appointment booking rules can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.
